text:
mia: Heads-up — enterprise customer (FinRegCo) pushed a contract ask: geo-failover with per-tenant isolation and an exemption clause for a subset of their workloads. We need a gating matrix + migration playbook to quote launch milestones and contract language.

alex: Do we have a canonical definition of 'per-tenant isolation' for this ask? e.g., strict hardware isolation, region-locked routing, or logical isolation with encryption-at-rest?

sam: From infra POV: the simplest path is region-locked routing + tenant slices (soft isolation) for now. Hardware isolation requires Dedicated pools and procurement lead time.

rachel: SRE note — any gating must include SLOs, failover timing, and rollback gates. Propose: readiness = 99.95% local region SLO, <200ms p95 intra-region, successful failover within 30s in staged test.

jenna: Legal: contract exemption needs precise scope. If FinRegCo wants an opt-out on routing fallbacks (e.g., never route to US from EU), we need to capture allowable exceptions (maintenance windows, emergency evacs) and carve those into SLA. Also need data residency attestation.

marco: Customer pushed this as a pre-buy condition for Dedicated. They accept price uplift but want firm launch dates and rollback protections. Sales expects Q3 delivery ask.

mia: Good context. Let's sketch a minimal gating matrix (proof-of-work -> canary -> full launch). I'm dropping a quick matrix, open to edits: 

```
gate,criteria,owner,acceptance
POC,teardown of routing tags + isolated prefix test,eng-runtime,pass deterministic test suite
CANARY,10 tenants in region with isolation routing,eng-platform,<1 incident in 72h
STAGED,50 tenants,full perf regression tests,eng-sre,<2 SLA violations in 7d
GA,production rollout to customer,product/legal,contract signoff + audits
```

alex: For the POC we should validate KV cache eviction and prefix caching correctness under isolation. Otherwise we'll get cross-tenant cache leakage.

sam: Agree. Also capacity reservations: we need a plan for burst capacity. For Dedicated we'd model 2x baseline for failover headroom. Ops will need a deployment window and runbook.

rachel: Add automated chaos tests to the canary gate: simulate node/region outage and measure failover correctness and time-to-recover. Capture metrics: failover_time, request_error_rate, tail_latency.

jenna: Also list the compliance artifacts needed for customer: data flow diagram, KMS controls, audit log retention policy, signed DPA addendum. We can't accept ambiguous exemption text.

marco: Customer also asked about billing segmentation during failover (they want invoice line-item for 'failover compute' vs standard). Finance will ask for a concrete metric to bill against.

mia: Next step: consolidate tech and legal acceptance criteria into a single acceptance doc we can attach to the quote. Draft owners: alex (architecture details), sam (capacity/runbook), rachel (SLO/chaos tests), jenna (contract language), marco (commercial terms).

alex: ETA for architecture doc — I can produce a draft in 4 business days. It will include routing policies, tag schema, and a fallback decision tree.

sam: I'll draft capacity model + runbook in 3 days. Need input from infra procurement if Dedicated hardware is chosen.

rachel: I'll sketch the SLO matrix and chaos scenarios in 2 days and prep the monitoring dashboards.

jenna: I'll prepare the contract clause templates and required artifacts list in 3 days.

marco: I'll sync with the customer and share the commercial constraints today; will push for Q3 target but flag that procurement/QA could slip.

mia: Important: decide whether we allow temporary 'contract exemptions' that are timeboxed vs permanent. My product view: prefer timeboxed pilot exemptions with explicit revocation triggers.

alex: Technical tradeoff: timeboxed exemptions are easier — we can implement feature flags scoped to tenant metadata. Permanent exemptions will require long-term policy/ops changes.

rachel: For launch criteria I'd insist on two separate gates: (1) safety (no cross-tenant data leakage) and (2) stability (SLOs for 7d). Both must pass.

sam: Ops question: who owns emergency evacs? If customer refuses fallback, we must still have a policy for catastrophic hardware failure. That needs C-level/legal signoff for risk acceptance.

jenna: We'll need a signed risk acceptance appendix for customers that opt out of certain fallbacks. Also add insurance/indemnity language.

mia: Sounds like we have alignment. I'll create a consolidated acceptance checklist and a short runbook skeleton. Proposed meeting: 48h working sync to review the draft gating matrix and acceptance doc. Who can join?

alex: I'm in.

sam: in

rachel: in

jenna: in

marco: in; will invite customer reps for the review.

deploy-bot: Meeting created: "Gating matrix & migration playbook review" — Thu 10:30am PT. Agenda: review POC/CANARY/STAGED/GA gates, legal artifacts, runbook owners. :calendar:

mia: Action items (short):
- alex: architecture draft (4d)
- sam: capacity + runbook (3d)
- rachel: SLO matrix + chaos tests (2d)
- jenna: contract clauses & artifact list (3d)
- marco: customer commercial constraints (today)

mia: I'll assemble the acceptance doc and ping everyone when drafts land. If we can get POC verification in 3 weeks, we can tentatively promise a staged pilot in 8-10 weeks, subject to procurement.

alex: One more tech note — we should also enumerate data residency enforcement points (ingest, storage, logs). I'll include that in the draft.

sam: Noted. Ops will need access controls for diagnostic logs to satisfy compliance.

rachel: I'll make sure the dashboards include tenant-scoped drift detection so we notice accidental cross-routing ASAP.

mia: Thanks all. We'll lock down the acceptance doc before the customer QBR.

marco: Thanks — I'll prep the customer expectations doc and include the tentative timeline.

jenna: Will add legal checklist to the meeting packet.

deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: review doc due in 48 hours.
